Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(a_{2026}=9\neq 0\), none of \(a_0,\dots,a_{2026}\) can be \(0\); otherwise the sequence would stay \(0\) forever. Thus we may take reciprocals.

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]

we get

\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}} \equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}.
\]

Rearranging,

\[
a_n \equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv
\frac1{a_{2027}}-\frac1{a_0}-2(2027)
\pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(a_0=1\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv
\frac1{a_{2027}}-1-4054
\pmod{397}.
\]

Now use \(a_{2026}=9\). The recurrence gives

\[
a_{2027}(9+1)^2 \equiv 9 \pmod{397},
\]

so

\[
100a_{2027}\equiv 9 \pmod{397}
\]

and therefore

\[
\frac1{a_{2027}}\equiv \frac{100}{9}\pmod{397}.
\]

Compute \(100/9\) modulo \(397\). Since

\[
9\cdot 364=3276\equiv 100 \pmod{397},
\]

we have

\[
\frac{100}{9}\equiv 364 \pmod{397}.
\]

Also,

\[
4054\equiv 84 \pmod{397}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
\equiv 279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
